whyNot: Source-Cluster Closure Batch 1 has one surviving cluster, 10.1038/s41580-020-00313-x, and all four of its open records are already members of the frozen 33-record Production package. A separate cluster canary would re-release the same four records under a second operation id, which is exactly the double-execution the replay-safe ids exist to prevent. The cluster is therefore canaried as part of the package, not beside it.

sequencing.observation: None of the four cluster records is in the package canary. All four are in the 28-record remainder.
sequencing.consequence: The five-record canary unlocks zero source pages. The source page for 10.1038/s41580-020-00313-x appears only once the remainder completes, because the aggregate gate refuses a page while any bound claim is unreleased.
sequencing.implication: Anyone checking for the new source route immediately after the canary will correctly find nothing. That is the gate working, not a failed release.
sequencing.verificationPoint: Check /knowledge/sources/10-1038-s41580-020-00313-x after the remainder, not after the canary.

expectedEffectWhenEventuallyExecuted.precondition: All five records bound to that source hold active releases. One already does; the remaining four are in the remainder.

boundary: A prepared plan. Nothing here has been executed and no release credential was used in producing it.
